nodes.name: Proposition 6.5: *+[F]+
nodes.statement:
Let $f\colon \mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{C}$ be given by a finite sum
\[
f\left(t\right)=\sum_{j\in J}c_{j}\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}p_{j}\left(t\right)},
\]
where the $c_{j}\in \mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}$ and the $p_{j}\left(t\right)$
are  distinct polynomials in $\mathbb{R}[t]$, vanishing at $0$. 
Then one can find $\varepsilon>0$ such that
\begin{enumerate}


\item 
There exist two sequences $\left(t_{0,n}\right)_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$  and $\left(t_{1,n}\right)_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$, which both tend to $+\infty$, 
such that $\forall n\in \mathbb{N}$, $\vert f\left(t_{0,n}\right)-f\left({t_{1,n}}\right) \vert \ge \varepsilon$.

 In particular  $\lim_{t\to+\infty}f\left(t\right)$ 
exists if and only if $p_{j}=0$ for all $j\in J$

(in other words, 

if and only if $f$ is a constant function).


\item 
 There exists
a sequence $\left(t_n\right)_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ which tends to $+\infty$ such that 
for all $n\ge 0$, $\vert f\left(t_n\right) \vert \ge \varepsilon$. 


\item  
$
\int_{V_{\varepsilon}}\frac{1}{t}\,\mathrm{d}t=+\infty,
$
where
$ V_{\varepsilon}=\{t\in[1,+\infty):\ \left|f\left(t\right)\right|\geq\varepsilon\}. $
\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Theorem 5.2: *+[F]+
nodes.statement:
\textbf{\emph{ }}Let $X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{m}$
be a subanalytic set and $f\in\mathcal{C}^{\exp}\left(X\times\mathbb{R}\right)$. Then there
exists a finite partition $\mathcal{A}$ of $X\times\mathbb{R}$ into cells over $\mathbb{R}^{m}$
such that for each $A\in\mathcal{A}$ that is open over $\mathbb{R}^{m}$, there exists
a centre $\theta$ for $A$ for which we may express $f\circ P_{\theta}$
as a finite sum
\[
f\circ P_{\theta}\left(x,y\right)=\sum_{j\in J}T_{j}\left(x,y\right)
\]
on $A_{\theta}=\{\left(x,y\right):\ x\in\Pi_{m}\left(A\right),a\left(x\right)<y<b\left(x\right)\}$, where each
$T_{j}$ is a generator for $\mathcal{C}^{\exp}\left(A_{\theta}\right)$, such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item if $b<+\infty$, then for each $j$, $T_{j}$ is superintegrable over
$\Pi_{m}\left(A\right)$;
\item if $b\equiv+\infty$, then there exists a positive integer $d$ and
a partition $J=J^{\mathrm{int}}\cup J^{\mathrm{naive}}$ such that:

\begin{enumerate}
\item for each $j\in J^{\mathrm{int}}$, $T_{j}$ is superintegrable over
$\Pi_{m}\left(A\right)$;
\item for each $j\in J^{\mathrm{naive}}$, $T_{j}$ is naive
in $y$, is not superintegrable over $\Pi_{m}\left(A\right)$ and is of the form
\begin{equation}
T_{j}\left(x,y\right)=f_{j}\left(x\right)y^{r_{j}}\left(\log y\right)^{s_{j}}\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}\phi_{j}\left(x,y\right)},
\end{equation}
where $f_{j}\in\mathcal{C}^{\exp}\left(\Pi_{m}\left(A\right)\right)$, $r_{j}\in\mathbb{Q}\cap[-1,+\infty)$,
$s_{j}\in\mathbb{N}$, and $\phi_{j}$ is a polynomial in $y^{1/d}$ (for
some $d\in\mathbb{N}$) with coefficients in $\mathcal{S}\left(\Pi_{m}\left(A\right)\right)$ such
that $\phi_{j}\left(x,0\right)=0$ for all $x\in\Pi_{m}\left(A\right)$; moreover,
\[
\left(\left(r_{j},s_{j},\phi_{j}\left(x,y\right)\right)\right)_{j\in J^{\mathrm{naive}}}
\]
is a family of distinct tuples in $\mathbb{Q}\times\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{R}[y^{1/d}]$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Theorem 2.20: *+[F]+
nodes.statement:
Let $f\in\mathcal{C}^{\exp}\left(X\times\mathbb{R}\right)$
for some subanalytic set $X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{m}$. Then there exists
$g\in\mathcal{C}^{\exp}\left(X\times\mathbb{R}\right)$ such that
\[
\mathrm{Int}\left(g,X\right)=X
\]
and
\[
f\left(x,y\right)=g\left(x,y\right),\quad\text{for all \ensuremath{x\in\mathrm{Int}\left(f,X\right)}\ and\ all \ensuremath{y\in\mathbb{R}}.}
\]
Moreover, $g$ can be written as a finite sum of generators for $\mathcal{C}^{\exp}\left(X\times\mathbb{R}\right)$
that are superintegrable over $X$.

Finally, there exists $h\in\mathcal{C}^{\exp}\left(X\right)$ such that
\[
\mathrm{Int}\left(f,X\right)=\{x\in X:h\left(x\right)=0\}.
\]

nodes.name: Proposition 2.19: *+[F]+
nodes.statement:
Let $f$ be a generator for $\mathcal{C}^{\exp}\left(X\times\mathbb{R}^{n}\right)$ that is superintegrable
over $X$, and define $F\colon X\to\mathbb{C}$ by
\[
F\left(x\right)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{n}}f\left(x,y\right)\,\mathrm{d}y.
\]
Then $F\in\mathcal{C}^{\exp}\left(X\right)$.

nodes.name: Theorem 2.12: *+[F]+
nodes.statement:
Let $f\in\mathcal{C}^{\exp}\left(X\times\mathbb{R}^{n}\right)$
for some subanalytic set $X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{m}$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$.
Then there exists $F\in\mathcal{C}^{\exp}\left(X\right)$ such that
\[
F\left(x\right)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{n}}f\left(x,y\right)\,\mathrm{d}y,\quad\text{for all \ensuremath{x\in\mathrm{Int}\left(f,X\right)}.}
\]

nodes.name: Remark 8.5: *+[F]+ Remark
nodes.statement:
Suppose that $\psi:X\times[0,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}^n$ is c.u.d.\ mod $1$ on $X$.  Then for each box $I \subseteq [0,1)^n$, there exists $k_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for all $k\geq k_0$, for all $x\in X$,
\[
\mathrm{vol}_1\left(  \{t\in[2^k, 2^{k+1}) :   \{ \psi\left(x,t\right)\}\in I\}  \right) 
\geq 2^{k-1}\mathrm{vol}_n\left(I\right).
\]
This bound is proven just as Lemma 6.3, using the uniform limit 
in the parameter $x$ provided by Definition 8.4.

nodes.name: Lemma 8.9: *+[F]+
nodes.statement:
With the notation just fixed above, we may express $f$ as a composition
\[
f\left(x,t\right) = F\left(x,\psi\left(x,t\right)\right)
\]
on $A$, where for some $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $\psi = \left(\psi_1,\ldots,\psi_n\right)$ is a monomial map in $t$ with analytic coefficient functions in $\mathcal{S}\left(\Pi_m\left(A\right)\right)$
and $F\left(x,z_1, \ldots, z_n\right)$ is 



a Laurent polynomial in the variables $\mathrm{e}^{2\pi \mathrm{i} z_1}, \ldots , \mathrm{e}^{2\pi\mathrm{i} z_n}$ 
with coefficients $f_j\left(x\right)$, $j\in J$. 
If $J$ is a singleton $\{j_0\}$ and if $\phi_{j_0} = 0$, then $n = 0$ and $F\left(x\right) = f_{j_0}\left(x\right)$.  
Otherwise we have
$n>0$ and 
\begin{enumerate}

\item there exists a set $B\subseteq \Pi_m\left(A\right)$ such that 
$\mathrm{vol}_m\left(\Pi_m \left(A\right) \setminus B\right)=0$
and for any $x\in B$,  $z\mapsto F\left(x,z\right)$ is nonconstant, 

\item
for any open set $\Omega\subseteq \Pi_m\left(A\right)$ and any real number $\lambda < \mathrm{vol}_m\left(\Omega\right)$, there exists a real number $T_0$ and a compact set $K\subseteq \Omega\cap B$ 
such that $K\times [T_0,+\infty)\subseteq A$, $\mathrm{vol}_m\left(K\right)\ge \lambda$ and $\psi\restriction{ K\times [T_0,+\infty)}$ is c.u.d. mod 1 on $K$. 
\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Proposition 8.7: *+[F]+
nodes.statement:
Consider a map $\psi = \left(\psi_1,\ldots,\psi_n\right):X\times[0,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}^n$, where $X$ is a compact topological space and where for each $j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$,
\[
\psi_j\left(x,t\right) = g_j\left(x\right) t^{\gamma_j}
\]
for some continuous function $g_j:X\to\mathbb{R}$ and positive integer $\gamma_j$.  Assume that for each $x\in X$, the functions $t\mapsto \psi_1\left(x,t\right),\ldots,t\mapsto\psi_n\left(x,t\right)$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$.  Then $\psi$ is c.u.d.\ mod $1$ on $X$.

nodes.name: Lemma 8.6: *+[F]+
nodes.statement:
Define $\phi:X\times [0,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ by
\[
\phi\left(x,t\right) = \sum_{j=0}^{d} \phi_j\left(x\right) t^j,
\]
where $d$ is a positive integer, the functions $\phi_0,\ldots,\phi_d:X\to\mathbb{R}$ are bounded, and there exists $\varepsilon > 0$ such that $|\phi_d\left(x\right)| > \varepsilon$ for all $x\in X$.  Then the function $\Phi:X\times[0,+\infty)\to\mathbb{C}$ defined by
\[
\Phi\left(x,T\right) = \int_{0}^{T} \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}\phi\left(x,t\right)}\,\mathrm{d}t
\]
is bounded.

\textbf{\emph{ }}Let $X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{m}$

nodes.name: Lemma 8.10: *+[F]+
nodes.statement:
Consider $f\left(x,t\right) = F\left(x,\psi\left(x,t\right)\right)$ as given in Lemma 8.9, with $z\mapsto F\left(x,z\right)$ nonconstant for some $x\in \Pi_m\left(A\right)$.  
Then there exist $\varepsilon>0$, 
$\delta > 0$,
a strictly increasing sequence $\left(t_j\right)_{j\in\mathbb{N}}$ in $\mathbb{R}$ diverging to $+\infty$, 
a compact set $K\subset X$ and a sequence $\left(X_j\right)_{j\in\mathbb{N}}$ of Lebesgue measurable subsets of $K \subseteq \Pi_m\left(A\right)$,
with for any  $j\in \mathbb{N}$, $\mathrm{vol}_m\left(X_j\right)\ge \delta$,  $ X_{2j+1}\subseteq X_{2j}$  and
such that
for all $j\in\mathbb{N}$, for all $x_0\in X_{2j}$, $x_1\in X_{2j+1}$, 
$$ 
\vert f\left(x_0,t_{2j}\right)\vert \ge \varepsilon
 \ \mathrm{ and } \ \vert f\left(x_0,t_{2j}\right) - f\left(x_1,t_{2j+1}\right)\vert \ge \varepsilon .$$

nodes.name: Proposition 8.2: *+[F]+
nodes.statement:
Let $p\in[1,+\infty]$ and $f\in\mathcal{C}^{\exp}\left(X\times\mathbb{R}\right)$
for a subanalytic set $X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{m}$, and suppose that $\left(f_{y}\right)_{y\in\mathbb{R}}$
is Cauchy in $L^{p}\left(X\right)$ as $y\to+\infty$. Then there exist $g\in\mathcal{C}^{\exp}\left(X\right)\cap L^{p}\left(X\right)$
and a subanalytic set $X_{0}\subseteq X$ such that $\mathrm{vol}_{m}\left(X\setminus X_{0}\right)=0$,
\[
\lim_{y\to+\infty}\|f_{y}-g\|_{p}=0,
\]
and
\[
\lim_{y\to+\infty}f\left(x,y\right)=g\left(x\right)\quad\text{for all \ensuremath{x\in X_{0}}.}
\]

nodes.name: Theorem 8.3: *+[F]+
nodes.statement:
Let $\widetilde{\hbox{\calli F}\ }$ be the
Fourier-Plancherel extension of the Fourier transform to $L^{2}\left(\mathbb{R}^{n}\right)$,
as in (6). Then, the image of $\mathcal{C}^{\exp}\left(\mathbb{R}^{n}\right)\cap L^{2}\left(\mathbb{R}^{n}\right)$
under $\widetilde{\hbox{\calli F}\ }$ is $\mathcal{C}^{\exp}\left(\mathbb{R}^{n}\right)\cap L^{2}\left(\mathbb{R}^{n}\right)$.
